slides.title: Draw the story first
slides.text: A story problem hides its math inside words. Draw the story as a bar, and the math steps out where you can see it.

slides.title: Bars show the pieces
slides.text: One long bar is the whole. Shorter bars under it are the parts. A part with no number yet gets a question mark. That mark is your job.

visual.label: A bar model: one whole bar split into a known part and an unknown part

focus.cue: The long bar is the whole story in one picture.
The part with no number gets a question mark. That mark is your job.

slides.title: Rough first, then draw
slides.text: Rough first: about 400 ribbons, minus about 150, leaves about 250. A shop had 386 ribbons and sold 147. Draw it.

visual.label: The ribbon story drawn: a whole bar of 386 ribbons, 147 sold, the rest left

focus.cue: One part is known: 147 ribbons sold.
The other part is the question: how many are left?

slides.title: The Jumble adds a gap
slides.text: The Jumble read a gap story and added instead of subtracting. Its bar showed two parts joining, but the story asked for a difference. Name the mistake before you fix it.

visual.label: The Jumble joined the parts; the story asked for the gap

rows.label: The Jumble's bar: two parts joining
The story's bar: a whole with a gap to find

focus.cue: The Jumble's bar joins two parts: it added.
The story asked for a difference: the gap is the unknown part.

words.means: a drawing of a story as bars for the whole and its parts
the full amount a story starts from
the answer to a subtraction: the gap itself

slides.title: Stretch: Two steps, two bars
slides.text: Some stories need two moves. Maya needs 500 points, has 275, and earns 90 more today. Draw one bar for what she still needs after today.

visual.label: Maya's two-step story in one bar: 500 points needed, 275 already, 90 more today, the rest still to earn

focus.cue: 275 points she has, and 90 more today: two known parts.
What is left of the 500 is still to earn: 135 points.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Brain Board at Practice Board and finish the whole board, every tile. It opens straight on your story board: every tile tells a story. Sketch each story as a bar before you pick an answer.
